# Project: AI-assisted UM Luxury Experience Mobile App

**Data last updated:** April 7, 2026  
**Team members:** Tuyara Chinbat  
**Project Status:** Ongoing

## Description

This project crafts a mobile app for UM football games to provide a VIP experience for high value individuals.

## Background and Problem Statement

**Background**

Academic research states that high-value individuals value extraordinary and personal experiences, temporal efficiency, and trusted personal relationships (2022). According to user interviews and student’s personal experiences, UM football games are filled with inefficiencies such as limited parking, high traffic outside and inside the stadium, and uncomfortable seating.

**Problem Statement**

The University of Michigan Athletic Department aims to increase football season ticket holder renewal rates by addressing the need for an enhanced, high-value digital experience for loyal high-value fans. These fans value VIP experiences that saves time and personalized services, such as pregame field access, but currently there is no such digital service available for them at the University of Michigan football games. The project should investigate what are the main pain points high value customers experience when attending a football game, what they value when having exclusive field access, and address them accordingly via a feasible, desirable, and viable single main view quick use app that acts as a digital ID and improves the overall gameday experience.

**Citations**

Klaus, Philipp ‘Phil’ (2022). "*What matters most to ultra-high-net-worth individuals? Exploring the UHNWI luxury customer experience (ULCX)*." [https\://www\.emerald.com/jpbm/article/31/3/368/449633/What-matters-most-to-ultra-high-net-worth](https://www.emerald.com/jpbm/article/31/3/368/449633/What-matters-most-to-ultra-high-net-worth). 

## Goals

* Offer a VIP experience for users that enables them to have exclusive field access and other perks such as seeing the performances up close  
* Help users figure out where the accessible seats are and what are accessible routes  
* Help users navigate the stadium to get to their seats/suites as well as to the field

### Target Audience and Personas 

This project targets high value football season ticket holders who have the capability to spend more money on football games and enjoy exclusive VIP experiences.

### Persona 1: Mike Miller

![][image1]

**Profession:** Software Engineer at a Tech company   
**Annual Income:** \$120,000  
**Age:** 25  
**Bio:** Mike is a software engineer in Detroit and he graduated from UoM in 2022\. He works hard and plays hard, work, networking, and partying. He likes to attend the football games for the camaraderie and the energy within the crowd during game days and he usually tailgates before heading to the games.

**Goals:**

1. Enjoy the energy and camaraderie of game day with his friends.  
2. Gain pregame field access and reconnect with his classmates on the field.

**Frustrations:**

1. UM team losing the football game and bringing down the vibes of the crowd.  
2. Narrow stairs that make it hard to go in and out of his seat during breaks to the bathroom or the concession stands.  
3. Watching the stadium tv monitor at a weird angle that hurts his neck.

### Persona 2: Gerald Price

**![][image2]**  
**Profession:** Lawyer  
**Annual Income:** \$170,000  
**Age:** 50  
**Bio:** Gerald is a divorced lawyer living in the Burns Park neighborhood of Ann Arbor. He is a UM alum and is a fan of the UM football team, and watches the games every season. He enjoys nice things and exclusive services. He is a busy person and time is his most valuable and scarce asset. He has bad knees. 

**Goals:**

1. Receive an exclusive and high end service at entertainment venues and services.  
2. Watch season games with a premium view with no blockages.

**Frustrations:**

1. Waiting in lines when entering the stadium or when purchasing from concession stands.  
2. Struggling going up and down stairs to get to his seat because his knees hurt.  
3. Finding his seat block in a big and crowded stadium.

### Persona 3: Jennifer Altman

![][image3]  
**Profession:** Stay-at-home mom, freelance writer  
**Annual Income:** \$74,000 (but her husband is rich)  
**Age:** 38  
**Bio:** Jennifer is a married stay-at-home mom with 2 children living in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Whenever she has time, she does freelance writing to help her husband with the financial wellbeing of the family. She is a UM alum and a huge fan of football, and watches home games every season with her family and deals with the stress of looking after them in a crowded environment. She is a busy mom with 2 children and a part time freelance role, so she values her free time a lot. 

**Goals:**

1. Taking advantage of the "VIP experience" to ensure her family is comfortable and entertained, and experience the game hassle-free.  
2. Buys the high-value tickets so she can take her children onto the field before the game to build their love for Michigan.  
3. Meeting her favorite player on her favorite team and taking a photo with them.

**Frustrations:**

1. Managing multiple tickets/passes for his family members and worrying about losing a physical credential.  
2. Waiting in line at concession stands and having her kids whining/crying.  
3. Managing family logistics in a crowded stadium.

## Core Features & Requirements

### In Scope:

1. Single main view app that acts as a digital ID for gameday entry into the stadium and field access.  
   1. Quick links for navigation to the seat and pregame field access   
      1. If a user presses on these quick links, they are navigated to the map section and the navigation to their selected item begins.  
   2. Aside from their own ID, the user should be able to view other tickets that they booked for their guests.  
      1. If the customer needs accessibility accommodations, it is clearly marked on their ticket.  
         1. The system realizes this and shows automatic accessible pathways on the map without the extra click of indicating.  
   3. A view of all the other tickets they hold for future games within the season.  
2. Interactive map of the stadium that shows seat blocks, accessible seating, field access entrance, user’s location.  
   1. There is a functional drawer that has buttons to navigate to their seat or pregame field access.  
      1. Information includes how many minutes it takes to navigate and directions.  
   2. Once the user clicks on the “navigate to the field” button the following shows:  
      1. The map shows the route that a person can take inside the stadium and generates the best path depending on foot traffic.  
      2. There is an option to choose an accessible route.  
      3. The drawer shows information about the step-by-step directions to the field.  
      4. There is an option to call for an escort.  
   3. Once the user clicks on the “navigate to your seat” button the following shows:  
      1. The map shows the route that a person can take inside the stadium and generates the best path depending on foot traffic.  
      2. There is an option to choose an accessible route.  
      3. The drawer shows information about the step-by-step directions to the field.  
      4. There is an option to call for an escort.  
   4. Real time notifications that inform which routes are less crowded and best to take at this time.  
3. There is personal staff that escorts them around the stadium from when they arrive, when they enter the field, and when they leave.  
   1. Chat function with escort is available through the app.  
4. The bottom navigation includes pathways to view tickets, map, profile.  
5. Profile section should include the following:  
   1. The user’s information  
   2. Their tier  
   3. Settings  
      1. This should include accessibility options for the user to indicate their accommodation preferences.

### Out of Scope:

1. Building the actual production-ready codebase or backend infrastructure for the University.  
2. Cross sport integrations outside of football games.  
3. Other 3 feature sets: parking, concession stand coupons, and bragging rights.

## Open Questions 

1. Where are the accessible seats in the stadium and are people able to sit with people they came with in those seats?  
2. How will we handle the map view of the stadium that includes different seat blocks, different levels, accessible seating and routes, and field access entrance?  
3. What are the current accessibility conditions at the stadium? Where are accessible seats located and what do the routes to them look like?

## Success criteria and metrics

**In the context of this class:**  
Build a fully functional, feasible, desirable, and viable app ready for release on the App Store using AI that encompasses all the necessary features.

**In the context of the app in general:**  
Reduce time spent locating their seat block by 30%.  
Increase football season ticket holder renewal rates by 15%.  
80% of users successfully use the app to access the pregame field experience.
